scope: Deterministic engine repair and trace replays. No new benchmark solver or judge calls.

source_evidence.input_export: Full recorded Iceberg materializations exported as CSV; row counts checked against saved snapshots. These are not sampled context rows.
source_evidence.input_export_limit: CSV round trips are not asserted to preserve every floating-point bit.

diagnosis.primary_cause: A cached-reader identity used URI and destination worker but omitted destination input port. Reusing one cached table on two ports overwrote the channel-to-port mapping, so one port never completed.
diagnosis.counterfactual_check: The original multi-port layouts also stalled with callbacks that only count input rows. The saved analysis callbacks fail immediately with column KeyErrors outside the engine.
secondary_issues: The one-to-one cached reader used the destination worker rather than its synthetic sender when constructing the partitioner. Python also passed an actor object where a name string was required.
Detached cached-reader failures were logged without delivering an error to the worker, leaving it waiting for input or completion.
Runtime statistics writes and close ran on different threads, racing inside the non-thread-safe Iceberg writer.
Forced sync termination could skip the final statistics callback, allowing workflow deletion before the writer closed.
The native diagnostic classifier matched timeout parameters in library tracebacks, labeling a 1.4-second FileNotFoundError as EXECUTION_TIMEOUT.

repairs: Include input port ID and internal flag in reader channel identities, consistently in Python/JVM registration, readers, and resource allocation.
Construct one-to-one partitioners with the synthetic sender identity in both runtimes.
Deliver detached reader failures through worker queues. Python uses a control channel so paused data cannot hide the failure; the JVM worker forwards it to its supervisor.
Serialize runtime statistics writes and final close on one executor, drain accepted writes, ignore late events, close once, and release the executor.
Flush statistics before every synchronous execution return, including console errors and deadlines.
Require explicit deadline evidence for EXECUTION_TIMEOUT and report cached read failures as CACHE_INPUT_READ with a storage recovery hint.

paired_live_replay.timing_definition: Seconds for the debug action, including execute/retrieve and reading the trace receipt; not isolated CPU time.
paired_live_replay.assertions: Exact rows on every port, every source CompletedFromCache, no execution timeouts, original callback KeyErrors surfaced, missing cache file reported promptly, same workflow succeeds after restoration.
paired_live_replay.fault_isolation: Only data files belonging to the newly created probe workflow were temporarily renamed; restored in finally before deleting probe resources.

statistics_log_check.scope: Final repaired stack after cached reads, callback failures, injected storage failure/recovery, history operations, and workflow deletion.

runtime_isolation.launch: bin/local-dev.sh; only the repair service was restarted
runtime_isolation.infrastructure: Existing private experiment database, storage, web and compiler services reused. Other development stacks and the old engine/agents were left running unchanged.

limitations: This establishes the cause and repair of the two reproduced multi-port layouts; it does not prove that every possible engine timeout is solved.
The original generated callbacks still contain incorrect input assumptions and column names. They now report those errors promptly; this engine change does not repair their analysis formulas.
No new LongDS accuracy, error-category reduction, or solver-cost improvement is claimed from these deterministic probes.
The first asynchronous statistics-close attempt still raced with table deletion. Final verification uses serialized close with an explicit synchronous-request flush.
next_experiment: Use this repaired engine for a short matched LongDS repeat, retain the existing solver prompts and judges, inspect the first divergence, and compare accuracy and cost before expanding.
